new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the first syllable; a rhythmic secondary stress falls on the following odd-numbered syllables (3rd, 5th). Stated for East (Konda) Mansi; Honti 1988: 151 states the same primary-stress rule in his description of Pelym (West) Mansi ('Die Betonung im Wogulischen ist dynamisch und liegt regelmäßig auf der ersten Silbe'), and Munkácsi 1887-90 (NyK 21: 325-326) gives it for all Vogul dialects except Tavda ('a vogulban általában a szó első tagjára esik a főhangsúly s a harmadikra a mellékhangsúly.. Ez általános hangsúly-törvénytől csak a tavdai nyelv tér el' = 'in Vogul generally the main stress falls on the first syllable of the word and the secondary stress on the third.. only the Tavda language deviates from this general stress law').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on odd-numbered non-initial syllables (Forsberg 2022); 'on the third syllable' (Munkácsi NyK 21: 325); Munkácsi NyK 23: 396 ties the Konda infinitive allomorphy (-γw in 2nd/4th vs -aγw in 3rd syllable) to this secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None in Forsberg 2022 or Honti 1988. Munkácsi (NyK 21: 326) adds that verbal prefixes take the stress off the base verb and negative/prohibitive particles off the following verb (phrase-level destressing), and that only Tavda (Southern Mansi, sout3253, not part of cent2322) deviates from the first-syllable law. Kulonen/Forsberg's English grammar notes phonetic shortening of first-syllable long vowels in closed syllables and before a long second-syllable vowel, without linking it to stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement (isolated word forms as transcribed in Kannisto's Konda texts); Munkácsi's remarks on prefixes and negative particles concern stress groups (hangsúly-egység) in connected speech.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog's 'Central Mansi' (cent2322) unites East Mansi (Konda: east2879, subdialects KU lowe1460, KM midd1374, KO uppe1481, Jukonda juko1234) and West Mansi (west2976: Pelym pely1234, Middle Lozva midd1373, Lower Lozva lowe1459, N/S Vagilsk). The quoted statement (Forsberg 2022) describes East Mansi, chiefly Middle and Lower Konda as recorded by Kannisto c. 1901-06 (language now extinct). Honti 1988: 151 gives the same first-syllable rule in a sketch of Pelym (West Mansi, pely1234), and Munkácsi 1887-90 states it for all Vogul dialects except Tavda (= Southern Mansi, sout3253, outside cent2322). Northern Mansi (mans1258) is a separate Glottolog language already handled elsewhere.

sources.note: Introduction pp. 325-326 (verified on page images NyK21_Munkacsi_p325-343/): in Vogul generally main stress falls on the first syllable and secondary stress on the third; verbal prefixes and negative/prohibitive particles take the stress off the following word; only the Tavda dialect deviates, so stress is marked per word only in Tavda. Munkácsi's own 1888-89 fieldwork covered N, Middle Lozva, Lower Lozva, Pelym, Konda, Tavda.

Notes long first-syllable vowels are realised semi-long/quarter-long in closed syllables and before a 2nd syllable with a long vowel.
